cumleler: Can looking at a light reduce nystagmus?
Fixation suppression: nystagmus decreases when the eye fixes on a point.
In this example, slow-phase velocity in darkness is twelve degrees per second.
Fixing on a light, the velocity drops to three degrees per second.
Peripheral nystagmus usually falls by over half; the cerebellum largely drives this.
Nystagmus not reduced by fixation suggests a central problem; inform the physician.
